judged_text: The computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] both evaluate to the literal property name "[object Object]" (the second silently overwriting the first), so minimumTokenResponseSchema is actually {access_token: string, "[object Object]": unknown} and the intended "any numeric property is the expiry" catch-all does not exist. In credential-sharing mode zod's default strip behavior removes every field except access_token from the parsed output, so expiry, instance_url, scope, token_type and refresh_token vanish from the data that every caller (office365, zoom, salesforce, google) persists — an operator who enables the sync env vars gets silently field-deleted credentials instead of synced ones.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined with computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. Those expressions are evaluated immediately to a single literal string key (not an index signature/catch-all), so they do not implement the intended “any numeric property is expiry” / “allow other properties” behavior. Since `z.object(...)` strips unknown keys by default, when credential-sharing mode selects `minimumTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(response)`, fields like `expiry_date`, `instance_url`, `scope`, `token_type`, etc. will be dropped from `.data`, and callers then persist/merge that stripped data (e.g. Office365 merges `tokenResponse.data`, Salesforce persists `accessTokenParsed.data`). This matches the finding’s claim of silent field deletion under the sync env vars.
